questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why famous people are often rejected many times before they finally succeed
An online trend of asking strangers for favours to get used to rejection
How therapists help socially anxious patients learn to talk to strangers
Why young people are spending much less time on social media than before
questions.why: They discuss 'rejection therapy', a social media trend where people film themselves asking strangers for favours.

questions.q: What is Neil's opinion of rejection at the start?
options: It gets easier with age, and it can even be a good thing
It is always harmful, so people should try to avoid it completely
It only really matters to people who are very shy by nature
He has never really experienced it himself in his life
questions.why: Neil says nobody likes it, but you get used to it as you get older and it's probably quite a good thing.

questions.q: Which of these did Hannah NOT ask a stranger?
options: To sit down at their table
To drive a taxi
To borrow some money
To take a nap in a bed in a shop
questions.why: She asked to sit at a table, to drive a cab and to try out a bed. She never asked for money.

questions.q: How did Hannah feel as she did more of these requests?
options: More nervous each time
Bored, because nobody said yes
Less worried each time, until the answer didn't matter to her
Angry at the people who refused
questions.why: The first one scared her, then each one 'came easier', and by the fourth she didn't mind if they said yes or no.

options: As a very shy person who hates talking to strangers
As a confident person who still felt scared at first
As a psychologist who studies rejection
As someone who films social media videos every day
questions.why: She says she isn't socially anxious and thinks she's really confident, but the first request really scared her.

questions.q: What criticism of rejection therapy videos do the presenters mention?
options: They are too long and boring to watch
They make people less confident
They are expensive to make
They film strangers, who might not want to be filmed
questions.why: Georgie says the videos involve filming interactions with strangers, which people might not want.

questions.q: According to psychologist Claudia Hammond, why might young people try this trend?
options: They are more worried about how others judge them
Their friends pay them to do it
Doctors recommend it as an official treatment
They want to become famous online
questions.why: She says perfectionism is increasing and young people worry more about how others judge them, so this may feel like a positive step.

questions.q: What did Hannah discover in the end?
options: Most people refused her requests
Rejection therapy is now a recognised treatment
Most strangers were friendly and happy to help
She became too nervous to finish the experiment
questions.why: Georgie says most strangers were friendly and happy to help, so Hannah hardly experienced rejection at all.
